threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 67 bus comes on time, don't you? It's more of a guideline than a schedule around here.
Caught a guy on the 196 last night belting out old grime tracks. Whole bus was vibing like it was a live show. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a group of kids turning a bus stop into a stage, performing a full show during the BVG strike—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find folks lining up for vegan currywurst at 3 AM, while the rest of the city winds down. It’s a late-night food pilgrimage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they actually know the difference between El Techo and its rooftop view versus the waiting line at La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a Muni driver hop out to chase down a stray dog on the tracks. Classic SF moment—only here do you find heart and chaos colliding.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals know they’re the heartbeats of neighborhood life, especially during the evenings.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the crosswalk—waiting for the green light even when it’s clear. Locals just walk.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers—they're the ones standing at the bus stop, confused, staring at the timetable like it's ancient hieroglyphs.
Caught the N37 last night; a group of art students turned the back seat into a makeshift sketch class. Hilarious to watch their chaotic creativity unfold.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy walking his pet ferret on a leash outside Spätkauf, I realized Neukölln truly has its own vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you stumble across a park where neighbors gather to swap books and pastries like they’re at a potluck. It’s the little communal acts that feel so uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: When you know that Muni delays are the urban version of a casual coffee break, you’re definitely from here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just witnessed a guy in a full tuxedo hop off a delayed bus, grab a slice from that corner pizza joint, and sprint to an event. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just a trendy photo spot, but it’s really the daily life of families packed into narrow streets, not just nightlife.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them standing confused at the metro ticket machines, ignoring the ‘T-10’ posters, and trying to pay for a single ride with cash.
